newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich says only minor issues left in budget talks.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich says only minor issues left in budget talks.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Sunday only minor issues remained to be resolved in balanced budget talks between the White House and Congress, saying a deal was possible Sunday "if we're lucky."

"I think we have an agreement, it's never done until it's done," Gingrich said as Republicans and administration officials prepared to begin another round of talks on tax and spending legislation to implement a five-year budget pact.

Congressional aides said the two sides were close, but cautioned there was still work ahead. Gingrich said the White House and Republicans were down to three "tiny" issues, one on taxes and two on spending, but was not specific.

The negotiators were returning to the bargaining table after congressional sources reported several key issues involving child care credits, capital gains tax rate cuts and child health insurance appeared near resolution.

Sources said both sides moved on one of the most contentious issues, a $500 per-child tax credit. Republicans are willing to make the credit available to more low-income workers as the White House wanted, while the administration appears ready to let families with incomes in excess of $60,000 claim the credit.

The White House and Republicans are trying to bridge differences in plans to give taxpayers an $85 billion tax cut over the next five years and make changes in domestic health social programmes to balance the budget by 2002.
